__meta.what: Golden file for splitByBps (src/core/units.ts). INV-6 and DET-1.
__meta.why: INV-6: every settled venture split sums exactly to its proceeds and the remainder is accounted, never dropped. A dropped remainder is how a ledger silently stops balancing, and it would not show up as an error - only as a total that quietly drifts.
__meta.remainder_rule: One minor unit per POSITIVE weight, in the order the weights were given, until the remainder is gone. A zero-weight role is skipped: it is owed no share, so it must receive no unit. Callers must pass weights in a canonical order (settlement uses venture_id then role_index), which is what makes INV-6 and DET-1 hold at the same time.
__meta.negative_zero: No entry is ever -0. applyBpsTrunc collapses Math.trunc(-0.5) (which is -0) to +0 at the source, so a -0 posting amount - equal to 0 under === but not Object.is - cannot reach a reconciliation keyed on the sign. The test still asserts the sum, which is the invariant that matters.
__meta.regenerate: The hand-authored columns are the oracle. To add a case: write it here with a deliberately wrong derived value, run the matching test in test/core, and copy the expected value out of the failure. Never paste engine output in without checking it against arithmetic you did yourself - that turns an oracle into a snapshot of a bug.

splits.note: the remainder carries the sign of the amount; the untouched trailing entry is +0, never -0 (applyBpsTrunc collapses it - see contract notes)

splits.name: zero_weight_gets_nothing
splits.note: a 0 bps role is owed no share, so the remainder skips it and lands on the first POSITIVE weight (index 1). Was a pinned defect that paid index 0; fixed in applyBpsTrunc's remainder loop.

splits.name: many_weights_max_remainder
splits.note: remainder is at most weights.length - 1, and all of it is allocated

splits.name: lopsided_weights
